plan.title: Alex finishes onboarding, moves the time, then commits (spec example; outside Eastern)

context.text: Yo! I'm ZOH. I'm gonna text you every day to help you start one thing and actually stick with it. Text "stop" anytime. What's your name, and what are you looking to work on?
alex. exercise, wanna get back to lifting
Let's go, Alex. Have you lifted before, and what did you usually do?
in college. home now, i have dumbbells
Dumbbells at home works. When are you usually free to get a workout in?
Love it. You can change how I coach you anytime, just tell me. Do you track your workouts anywhere, like a watch or an app?

transcript.text: Last thing before I build your plan, Alex: what city are you in? It helps me get your 7:30 am timing right.
Denver, got it. Where do you want this to get you, Alex? Like lifting a certain weight, a certain look, or just feeling strong again? Not sure yet is fine too.
not sure yet. just wanna feel strong again and get the lifting back

Feeling strong again is a solid place to start, Alex. Here's the plan:
• Headed for: feeling strong and getting lifting back in your routine
• Day 1 (tonight, 7:30 pm, 20 min): 3 rounds of 10 goblet squats, 10 one-arm rows per side, and 8 to 10 floor presses. Pick weights that feel like a 6 or 7 out of 10.
• Usual schedule: 7:30 am, 20 min, Mon to Fri, at home. I'll text you a heads-up at 7:20 am.
• Proof: a photo of your dumbbells and workout space right after you finish. A quick voice note works too.
• Why: easy full-body moves rebuild your form and habit first, then we add weight.

Each day's workout shapes the next one, so it gets harder as you get stronger. What do you think?

Easy, 7 it is. Starting earlier means more of the day is yours. Here's the updated plan:
• Headed for: feeling strong again and getting lifting back
• Day 1 (tonight, 7:00 pm, 20 min, at home): 3 rounds of 10 goblet squats, 10 one-arm rows per side, and 8 to 10 floor presses. Pick weights that feel like a 6 or 7 out of 10.
• Usual schedule: 7:00 am, 20 min, Mon to Fri. I'll still reach you with a heads-up at 6:50 am.
• Proof: a photo of your dumbbells and workout space right after you finish. A voice note works too.
• Why: easy full-body moves rebuild your form and habit first, then we add weight.

Each workout shapes the next one, so it gets harder as you get stronger. What do you think?
LET'S GO, Alex! 💪 Day 1 is tonight at 7:00 pm: goblet squats, rows and floor presses. Send me that photo when you're done.

conversation.reason: 'Last thing before I build your plan' is followed by a destination question, so the plan-needed questions came after a 'that's everything' line.
Concrete exercises, reps, home, 7:30 am and photo proof, though weights are only effort-based and the Mon to Fri days were assumed.

grade.summary: ZOH built a concrete, well-shaped plan quickly and handled the time revision and lock cleanly, with a day 1 step and proof that fit the tester. The main misses are an invented Mon to Fri schedule, a 'Last thing' line followed by another question, and no explicit commitment ask before the tester's 'im in'.
